sophie (support): Heads up — customer on Dedicated (eu-prod-gpu) reports dashboard shows 0 GPUs for all nodes after we ran the cluster rename earlier today. Console lists nodes but GPU column is empty, and the customer sees API errors when creating jobs. Ticket #12345. Anyone seen this?

emma (eng-sre): Thanks, can you paste the exact cluster name and any recent infra changes? also output of `kubectl get nodes -o wide` from their control plane if available.

sophie (support): Cluster was renamed from `eu-west-gpu-1` -> `eu-prod-gpu` at 08:12 UTC. Attached brief output from their control plane: 
```
NAME                STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION
node-01             Ready    worker   12d   v1.25.4
node-02             Ready    worker   12d   v1.25.4
node-03             Ready    worker   12d   v1.25.4
```
But dashboard shows GPU count 0 for each node. They also get 422 from the jobs API when selecting GPU resource.

leo (obs): Could be the inventory service not picking up the node gpu labels after rename. Check the inventory metrics: `redwood.inventory.node_gpus` and the last scrape time. I can check from observability.

leo (obs): Observability snippet: 
```
redwood.inventory.node_gpus{cluster="eu-prod-gpu"} 0
redwood.inventory.node_scrape_timestamp{cluster="eu-prod-gpu"} 1.7665011e+09
```
Looks like the last successful scrape was ~10s after the rename but with 0 gpus.

raj (platform): We did a terraform apply that renamed the cluster (commit 0a9d3). The inventory-agent relies on a label selector `cluster=eu-west-gpu-1` in the agent config. Migration patched the cluster name in k8s, but the agent config in the dedicated control plane wasn't updated, so it probably filtered out GPU labels.

emma (eng-sre): That would explain it — agent was still scraping with old selector and falling back to an empty set. Can you check the inventory-agent configmap? `kubectl -n redwood-dedicated get cm inventory-agent-config -o yaml`

raj (platform): Confirmed configmap still had `cluster: eu-west-gpu-1`. I just opened a quick fix to patch it to `eu-prod-gpu`. Patch command I ran locally: 
```
kubectl -n redwood-dedicated patch cm inventory-agent-config -p '{"data":{"cluster":"eu-prod-gpu"}}'
```

deploy-bot: deploy/inventory-agent v2026.03.17-0a9d3 promoted to prod by raj at 08:45 UTC :rocket:

emma (eng-sre): After patching, we need to force a re-sync. Can you restart the inventory-agent deployment? `kubectl -n redwood-dedicated rollout restart deployment/inventory-agent`

sophie (support): Ran the restart and asked the customer to refresh the dashboard. They reported GPU counts returning within ~30s.

sophie (support): Quick reproducible steps for follow-up incident ticket: 
1) Rename cluster via infra (terraform).
2) If inventory-agent configmap not updated by migration hooks, agent will keep old label selector and report zero GPUs.
3) Symptoms: dashboard shows nodes present but GPU column 0, jobs API returns 422 when requesting GPUs, `redwood.inventory.node_gpus` metric 0.

emma (eng-sre): Action items: 
- Platform: add migration step to update inventory-agent configmap or make agent read cluster name from cluster CRD instead of hardcoded cm.
- Devex/Deploy: add a post-apply hook in terraform to run a configmap sync job.
- Observability: add an alert when `node_scrape_timestamp` < now-5m OR when `node_gpu_ratio` drops to 0 while node count >0.

raj (platform): I'll open infra PR to add the post-apply configmap patch and a small canary check that validates GPU labels exist after rename.

leo (obs): I'll add a short-run Grafana panel to highlight cluster rename mismatches and wire an alert for the scrape age.

emma (eng-sre): Temporary mitigation documented: run `kubectl -n redwood-dedicated patch cm inventory-agent-config -p '{"data":{"cluster":"<new-name>"}}'` and `kubectl -n redwood-dedicated rollout restart deployment/inventory-agent`. I'll add these two commands to the runbook.

sophie (support): Customer closed the incident after counts returned. Marking ticket #12345 resolved. Will follow up with customer-facing postmortem next week. :white_check_mark:
file_notes: created for dedicated capacity dashboard inventory gap post-rename
